# Ask my blog

> Semantic search over Tushar Kanjariya's Medium posts that runs entirely in the browser. The all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embedding model (about 23 MB) runs through Transformers.js. There is no API key, no backend and no vector database, and it works offline after the first load.

Key facts:

- 253 posts are split into 3,718 sections. Each section is a 384-dimension embedding, stored as int8 in a 1.4 MB file (`vectors.bin`).
- The browser embeds only the reader's question, then scores every section with a dot product. Each post's best section wins.
- A search takes about 40 ms on a desktop CPU over WebAssembly and makes zero network calls.
- Accuracy test: the right post ranks first for 35 of 38 real reader questions, and in the top 3 for 37.
- New posts come from the Medium RSS feed through a scheduled GitHub Action.

## Links

- [Live demo](https://tusharkanjariya.github.io/browser-ai-demo/): the search page
- [Source code](https://github.com/TusharKanjariya/browser-ai-demo): static site, Node build scripts and the accuracy test
- [README](https://github.com/TusharKanjariya/browser-ai-demo#readme): how it works, numbers, limitations
- [Author on Medium](https://medium.com/@TusharKanjariya): Tushar Kanjariya, full-stack developer writing about AI tooling and web development

## Data files

- [posts.json](https://tusharkanjariya.github.io/browser-ai-demo/posts.json): post titles, subtitles, links, dates and key terms
- [chunks.json](https://tusharkanjariya.github.io/browser-ai-demo/chunks.json): one row per section (post id, anchor, heading, short snippet)
